0|4679b61f2640e07724507fcd9dc070517bc6e6cb|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: x86: never trap MSR_KERNEL_GS_BASE
KVM has an old optimization whereby accesses to the kernel GS base MSR
are trapped when the guest is in 32-bit and not when it is in 64-bit mode.
The idea is that swapgs is not available in 32-bit mode
guest has no reason to access the MSR unless in 64-bit mode and
32-bit applications need not pay the price of switching the kernel GS
base between the host and the guest values.
However
column2: this optimization adds complexity to the code for little

column1: benefit (these days most guests are going to be 64-bit anyway) and in fact
broke after commit 678e315e78a7 (""KVM: vmx: add dedicated utility to
access guest's kernel_gs_base""
can be corrupted across SMIs and UEFI Secure Boot is therefore broken
(a secure boot Linux guest
column3: fails to reach the login prompt

column1: about half the time).  This patch just removes the optimization; the
kernel GS base MSR is now never trapped by KVM
GS base MSRs.
